correctness.rationale: For each finite dimension, strictly decreasing adjacent crossing times make unique exponent maxima switch in prescribed order. Four consecutive observation snapshots around each crossing converge after normalization to eigenvectors v_(j+1),v_(j+1),v_j,v_j; orthogonality forces 0/1/0 limits of the sine residual. Continuity in the finite lag gives strict maxima at all m-1 indices simultaneously. A contraction argument with the previous scalar minimizer shows E(s+1)<=exp(-L nu_1)E(s) for every s. Direct independently implemented modal-weight numerical comparisons passed 273 assertions across m=2..8, but do not substitute for the all-m proof.

value.rationale: The sharp 0/1/0 limiting pattern proves that absolute burn-in contraction alone cannot justify relative one-delay forecasting reliability, even for the canonical one-dimensional Dirichlet heat matrix. The number of severe reliability reversals is unbounded with grid dimension. This boundary distinguishes absolute error guarantees in a recent semigroup-delay closure analysis from genuinely normalized performance, while explicitly delimiting contrived nonlocal observations.
